[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L5 adds gut-wall efflux and intestinal-metabolism experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for presystemic loss, with direction and experimental context preserved; mechanism alone is not a direct oral-bioavailability result.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: KNI-272, the closest transferable gold context, showed direct human absolute oral bioavailability of 29.56±3.50% (4 mg/kg fasted capsule), 33.48% (6.6 mg/kg fasted capsule), 54.97±19.78% (10 mg/kg fasted capsule), 33.99±9.73% (2 mg/kg fasted capsule), and 36.40% (6.6 mg/kg fed capsule); the query shares the hydroxyethylamine, tert-butyl carboxamide, and cysteine-thioether motif.

Additional KNI-272 capsule values remained above 20% (31.13±12.98% at 14 mg/kg fasted; 22.06±2.99% at 4 mg/kg fed), while cherry-syrup formulations lowered F to about 15-20%, indicating formulation sensitivity rather than a scaffold-level F<20% outcome.

L5 saquinavir records show saquinavir is a P-gp substrate (efflux ratio >2 in Caco-2/MDCK-MDR1) with substantial intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism (human intestinal microsome intrinsic clearance 0.6-8.8 ml/min/mg), and P-gp inhibition increases saquinavir absorption/exposure; this is mechanistic presystemic-loss evidence for saquinavir, not a direct F measurement for the query.

The query differs from saquinavir at the N-terminal/P2 region (hydroxy-methylbenzoyl-S-benzyl cysteine vs quinoline-asparagine-phenylalanine) and is closer to KNI-272 there; KNI-272 achieved F 22-55% in humans despite the same HIV-protease-inhibitor class, so the saquinavir mechanism does not overturn the KNI-272-based high prediction.

L4 saquinavir absorption records (Caco-2 Papp 4.68±0.34 ×10^-5 cm/s, mesylate solubility ~2.2 mg/mL, rapid dissolution) support an adequate intestinal absorption component, but do not measure first-pass loss.
No L5 record provides an absolute F <20% for the query or a close analog; mechanism alone is insufficient to predict low.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule.
L5 records are saquinavir-specific mechanistic data (P-gp efflux, intestinal CYP3A4), not query-specific; query P-gp/CYP3A4 substrate status is unmeasured.
Saquinavir unboosted absolute F is not directly reported in the supplied records; L3 exposure data are exposure-only without IV comparator.
KNI-272 direct F values are in patients at mg/kg doses with specific capsule/syrup formulations; query formulation and dose are unknown.
The impact of the decahydroisoquinoline-for-thiazolidine and S-benzyl-for-S-methyl differences on P-gp/CYP3A4 liability is not directly measured.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high because the closest endpoint-matched evidence, KNI-272, has direct human absolute F of 22-55% for capsule formulations and the query shares the hydroxyethylamine/tert-butyl amide/cysteine-thioether scaffold. L5 saquinavir P-gp/CYP3A4 records add mechanistic concern for presystemic loss but are not direct F measurements and do not overturn the KNI-272 outcome; no affirmative threshold-relevant evidence supports F<20% for the query.
